topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing for the lecture, introducing the lecturer, the course context, and the primary learning outcomes regarding cancer etiology and carcinogens.

topics.label: Intrinsic and Environmental Determinants of Cancer Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer etiology by examining how intrinsic genetic mutations, endogenous metabolic errors, lifestyle factors, and epidemiological variations combine to influence cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and the Burkitt Lymphoma Paradigm
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogens contribute to oncogenesis, highlighting Denis Burkitt's epidemiological findings and the cooperative mechanisms between malaria and Epstein-Barr virus in driving Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how physical radiation and dietary or industrial chemicals undergo metabolic activation to induce direct DNA adducts, transversions, and oxidative damage.

topics.label: Tumor Initiation versus Promotion in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics differentiate between direct DNA-damaging initiators and non-mutagenic promoters that drive cancer development through chronic inflammation and proliferative signaling pathways.

topics.label: Host Context, Developmental Susceptibility, and Mechanistic Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how developmental timing and hormonal context influence susceptibility to carcinogens before summarizing the core biological mechanisms of carcinogenesis presented in the lecture.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe genomic mutational signatures, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo animal models, and the in vitro Ames test used to identify and evaluate carcinogenic agents.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk–Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing of the lecture, summarizing the main takeaways on environmental cancer risks and personal risk–benefit decisions.
